name: Materials Characterization
description: The measurement and analysis of the structure, composition, and properties of materials.

name: Metallurgy
description: The science of metals, their extraction, alloying, and processing.

name: Ceramics
description: The science of inorganic non-metallic materials formed by heating.

name: Polymer Materials
description: The materials science of synthetic and natural polymeric substances.

name: Composite Materials
description: Engineered materials combining two or more distinct phases for enhanced properties.

name: Semiconductor Materials
description: Materials with controllable electrical conductivity used in electronics.

name: Nanomaterials
description: Materials engineered at the nanometer scale with size-dependent properties.

name: Biomaterials
description: Materials designed to interact safely with biological systems.

name: Functional Materials
description: Materials with engineered electrical, magnetic, optical, or responsive functions.

name: Computational Materials Science
description: The modeling and simulation of material structure and properties.

name: Materials Synthesis
description: The processes by which materials are fabricated and processed.

name: Electron Microscopy
description: Imaging of materials using electron beams at very high resolution.

name: Transmission Electron Microscopy
description: Electron microscopy in which the beam transmits through a thin specimen for atomic-scale imaging.

name: Scanning Electron Microscopy
description: Electron microscopy rastering a focused beam to image surface topography.

name: X-Ray Diffraction
description: The use of X-ray scattering to determine crystal structure and phase composition.

name: Mechanical Testing
description: The measurement of strength, hardness, and deformation of materials.

name: Surface Analysis
description: Techniques for characterizing material surfaces and thin films.

name: Physical Metallurgy
description: The study of metal structure-property relationships and phase transformations.

name: Extractive Metallurgy

name: Ferrous Metallurgy
description: The metallurgy of iron and steel production.

name: Non-Ferrous Metallurgy
description: The metallurgy of metals other than iron, such as copper and aluminum.

name: Powder Metallurgy
description: The production of metal parts by compacting and sintering metal powders.

name: Mechanical Metallurgy
description: The study of metal deformation, strengthening, and failure.

name: Corrosion Science
description: The study of the degradation of metals by chemical and electrochemical attack.

name: Alloy Design
description: The design of new metal alloys with tailored properties.

name: Traditional Ceramics
description: Clay-based ceramics used in pottery, brick, and porcelain.

name: Advanced Ceramics
description: High-performance ceramics engineered for structural and electronic applications.

name: Structural Ceramics

name: Electronic Ceramics
description: Ceramics with electrical, dielectric, or piezoelectric functions.

name: Glass Science
description: The study of the structure, properties, and processing of glassy materials.

name: Refractory Materials
description: Materials resistant to very high temperatures used in furnaces and kilns.

name: Cement and Concrete Science
description: The chemistry and properties of cementitious construction materials.

name: Polymer Engineering
description: The processing and design of polymer materials into products.

name: Elastomers

name: Smart Polymers

name: Metal-Matrix Composites
description: Composites of reinforcements within a metal matrix.

name: Ceramic-Matrix Composites
description: Composites of ceramic fibers within a ceramic matrix for high-temperature use.

name: Fiber-Reinforced Composites

name: Nanocomposites
description: Composites incorporating nanoscale fillers for enhanced properties.

name: Organic Electronics

name: Optoelectronic Materials

name: Photovoltaic Materials
description: Materials that convert sunlight into electricity in solar cells.

name: Thermoelectric Materials
description: Materials that convert temperature differences into electrical voltage.

name: Superconducting Materials
description: Materials that conduct electricity without resistance below a critical temperature.

name: Carbon Nanomaterials
description: Nanoscale allotropes of carbon with exceptional properties.

name: Graphene
description: A single layer of carbon atoms in a hexagonal lattice with remarkable strength and conductivity.

name: Carbon Nanotubes
description: Cylindrical carbon molecules with exceptional tensile strength and electronic properties.

name: Fullerenes
description: Hollow carbon molecules such as the buckminsterfullerene C60.

name: Nanoparticles
description: Particles between 1 and 100 nanometers with size-dependent properties.

name: Nanostructured Materials
description: Bulk materials whose properties are defined by nanoscale internal structure.

name: Nanofabrication
description: The manufacturing of structures and devices at the nanoscale.

name: Quantum Dots
description: Semiconductor nanocrystals with size-tunable optical and electronic properties.

name: Implant Materials

name: Tissue Engineering Materials

name: Biocompatibility

name: Drug Delivery Materials

name: Ferroelectric Materials

name: Piezoelectric Materials

name: Energy Storage Materials

name: Shape Memory Alloys

name: Photonic Materials
description: Materials that manipulate light through periodic structures or optical properties.
